description: The main window on desktop: self-update and relaunch (UPD-001-006), the process log and its folder (LOG-008), and the Sharing settings pane for Remote Login and Screen Sharing (R-059, R-079; it fails as unavailable on Linux), and this computer's name, OS user, OS, VPN address and whether SSH answers there, to fill in Add device (R-058, R-060), whether the app carries the metrics agent and installing it for this user with an enrolment code and the hub origin, both checked by the shell, which takes no path or program (MET-019, D-10 d), whether the app carries the hub's programs and installing, removing and reading the state of the hub on this computer for this user, which take no argument at all (one-click plan S4), starting and stopping that hub, reading its operator account, making a TOTP secret, making the account with the secrets passed on to the hub's program on standard input only and where the replacement of an existing account runs only after a native confirmation dialog of that one request, which script cannot answer, and saving a copy of the hub's key through a native save dialog so that the key never reaches the web view (S6 F-4, F-9, 2.8), joining this device to a hub with an invite whose form the shell checks, the device link's state and leaving the hub (S6 2.6), and whether a process of this user listens on a hub address `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (S6 F-10). The dialog plugin's own permissions are granted to no web view. Then the state of the `anima` command line tool on the PATH and installing or removing its link or launcher, which takes only the folder the shell proposed (INS-004 to INS-006), the permissions of the `anima mcp` server for a hub, read and saved in the command line's configuration file on this computer, which take no path and no token (MCP-018), the stay-awake control of this computer: read it, choose one of its three levels, set its battery floor, and start or remove the set-up step of the lid-closed level, which take no program, path or command (AWK-001 to AWK-008), and the device web views: open, place, show, step, pin, pop out and close them, read a leaf certificate and open an address in the system browser (WEB-004–008, D-9). Device web views (labels `web-<tab id>`) are named by no capability, so they have no IPC (WEB-007, D-3); keep every capability on `"webviews": ["main"]`, with no `windows` and no `remote`. The updater and process plugins are registered in release builds only, so in a debug build their permissions grant nothing. Known width: a script in the web view may pass headers, timeout, proxy and target to check, and may relaunch the app; it cannot change the key, the endpoints or the downgrade rule (WP-04b final review C-1).
